words: 0.4.2 adds one optional column, market_value_eod_claim (measured or inferred), required on every PRESENT Orion row and null on an ABSENT row; the contract's optional_columns gains that sixth entry and the enums block gains its enum. The 19 columns, their types, schema_hash, every earlier enum and the five earlier optional columns are byte-identical; served_day_rules, source_requires and source_rules are unmoved, and rule24_record keeps every earlier key and adds v042. Every earlier NON-Orion writer still validates, with or without the claim. An Orion writer must now carry the claim on a PRESENT row: a 0.4.1 Orion row without it no longer validates, by the CTO's rule. The one Orion writer, the Scope adapter, already writes the claim (surprise row IRPT_DASHBD-D2-W223-S1). The 0.4.0, 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 test files all pass; the 0.4.1 file took a bounded amendment (its validator reads required_unless_absent and its PRESENT Orion fixtures carry the claim). NOT PROVEN: that the Scope adapter writes the claim as the contract declares it, that its parquet output validates against this contract, or that any consumer rejects an inferred value.
